      "subject": "Family stories for the cookbook",
      "content": "Hi Lakshmi,\n\nI've been testing recipes and building out the pages for the cookbook. Appa's tamarind sambar turned out great on my third try -- had to dial back the tamarind and add a bit more jaggery, just like you said.\n\nI want to add a narrative section to each recipe. A short paragraph about the story behind the dish, something personal that Priya can read alongside the recipe. Here's what I'm thinking:\n\nFor Appa's sambar -- the Sunday morning ritual, how he'd start the toor dal while listening to MS Subbulakshmi. Do you remember any other details?\n\nFor Amma's biryani -- I remember her making it for Diwali and other occasions. Was there a specific time you remember most?\n\nFor Paati's mango pickle -- I barely remember her making it, I was too young. You were older so you probably have better memories. Anything about her process, or why she was so particular about the mangoes being the right shade of green?\n\nIf you have other recipes we should include, let me know. I'm aiming for 8-10 total. Planning to send everything to a print service by early April.\n\nThanks,\nArjun",
      "cc": [],
      "parent_id": null,
      "attachments": {},
      "timestamp": 1773366300.0,
      "is_read": true
    },
    {
      "email_id": "9a3325c955fbec3bf8c0ff0c",
      "folder": "INBOX",
      "sender": "lakshmi.srini@gmail.com",
      "recipients": [
        "arjun.srinivasan@gmail.com"
      ],
      "subject": "Re: Family stories for the cookbook",
      "content": "omg Arjun these are going to be SO good\n\nok so for the sambar -- yes the Sunday ritual was everything. He'd wake up before anyone else and you could smell the toor dal from upstairs. And it wasn't just MS Subbulakshmi, he also played Balamuralikrishna when he was feeling fancy lol. He always said the secret was patience, you can't rush the tamarind. Also remember how he used to taste it like 10 times and adjust the salt every time? Mom used to get annoyed because he'd use every spoon in the kitchen.\n\nFor the biryani -- the one I remember most is Diwali 2008. We had like 20 people over and Amma made this MASSIVE pot. She was up at 5am prepping the chicken marinade. The whole house smelled like saffron and fried onions. I think that was also the year you burned your hand trying to help with the birista.       "content": "Hi Lakshmi,\n\nI've been testing recipes and building out the pages for the cookbook. Here's what I'm thinking:\n\nFor Appa's sambar -- the Sunday morning ritual, how he'd start the toor dal while listening to MS Subbulakshmi. Was there a specific time you remember most?\n\nFor Paati's mango pickle -- I barely remember her making it, I was too young. You were older so you probably have better memories.       "subject": "Re: Family stories for the cookbook",
      "content": "omg Arjun these are going to be SO good\n\nok so for the sambar -- yes the Sunday ritual was everything. He'd wake up before anyone else and you could smell the toor dal from upstairs. And it wasn't just MS Subbulakshmi, he also played Balamuralikrishna when he was feeling fancy lol. He always said the secret was patience, you can't rush the tamarind. Also remember how he used to taste it like 10 times and adjust the salt every time? Mom used to get annoyed because he'd use every spoon in the kitchen.\n\nFor the biryani -- the one I remember most is Diwali 2008. We had like 20 people over and Amma made this MASSIVE pot. She was up at 5am prepping the chicken marinade. The whole house smelled like saffron and fried onions. I think that was also the year you burned your hand trying to help with the birista. You were like 13.\n\nFor Paati's pickle -- ok so I remember a lot actually. She was VERY particular about the mangoes. They had to be tottapuri variety, hard and sour, no yellow spots at all. She'd go to like three different markets to find the right ones. And the mustard oil had to be heated and cooled three times before she mixed it in. She said it removed the bitterness. The jar sat in the sun on the balcony for 7-8 days and nobody was allowed to touch it. She said if you opened the lid before it was ready it would spoil. I was terrified of it as a kid lol.\n\nOther recipes you should add:\n- Amma's rasam (the one with pepper and garlic, not the restaurant kind)\n- Appa's coconut chutney (so simple but nobody else gets it right)\n- Paati's murukku (you probably don't remember these but she made them for every festival)\n\nLet me know if you need more!\n\n- Lakshmi",
